references.text: Earlier in the chapter, Zebah and Zalmunna fled, and Gideon pursued them. This verse describes the beginning of the pursuit that culminates in their execution.
Gideon asked for bread for his men while he was pursuing Zebah and Zalmunna, the Midianite kings whom he eventually kills in verse 21.
The crescent ornaments (sahароним) that Gideon took from the camels' necks are mentioned again here as part of the war plunder from the Midianites.
Israel killed Midianite kings in battle, an earlier example of killing enemy kings like Zebah and Zalmunna.
Joshua killed the five kings and hung them on trees, a similar example of an Israelite leader executing defeated kings.
The psalm mentions Zebah and Zalmunna by name as examples of God's enemies who were defeated.
Crescent ornaments (sahароним) are mentioned as jewelry worn by the women in Jerusalem, the same type of ornament that Gideon took from the camels.
